titleZh: 埃隆·马斯克的SpaceX工厂参观之旅（霍桑，2010年）
summaryEn: Elon Musk walks visitors through the SpaceX headquarters in Hawthorne, California — the 500,000 sq ft former Boeing 747 plant where SpaceX designs and builds about 80% of the Falcon line. Filmed in 2010, just weeks before Dragon became the first privately built spacecraft to orbit and return; this walkthrough of the offices and factory floor is the tour widely associated with Musk showing young founders around the plant.
summaryZh: 埃隆·马斯克带领访客参观SpaceX位于加利福尼亚州霍桑的总部——这座占地500,000平方英尺的工厂前身是波音747工厂，SpaceX在这里设计并制造猎鹰系列约80%的部件。视频拍摄于2010年，当时距离龙飞船成为首艘进入轨道并返回的私营企业建造航天器仅有数周；这段对办公室和工厂车间的参观视频，就是人们普遍认为马斯克带年轻创始人参观工厂的那次行程。

segments.textEn: All [Music] right, welcome to SpaceX. Uh, here we are in the lobby. It's very white right now, but there are actually some some cool uh elements coming in soon that will make it less white. In the front of the building, we have our engineering offices and and space for about 300 people per floor. And we've got a total of about three floors that we can open. Right now, only the first floor is occupied. Um we try to aim for something which is a very open plan uh to maximize communication and make it sort of you know fairly nicel looking. Uh this place used to be quite dismal. That's that's my office over there. Actually we really try to minimize the number of offices that we have because doors limit communication. Everyone at the company with the exception of a few people in like HR and finance actually um are in cubes uh including your vice presidents over there. There's Gwen at her cube.
segments.textZh: 好吧，[音乐]欢迎来到 SpaceX。呃，我们现在在大厅。这里现在非常白，不过实际上很快会加入一些很酷的，呃，元素，让它不那么白。大楼前部是我们的工程办公室，每层可容纳约 300 人。我们总共大约有 3 层可以启用。目前只有第 1 层有人办公。嗯，我们力求采用非常开放的布局，呃，以最大限度地促进沟通，也让这里看起来算是，你知道，相当漂亮。呃，这地方以前相当阴沉。那边就是我的办公室。实际上，我们确实尽量减少办公室的数量，因为门会限制沟通。公司里除了人力资源和财务等部门的少数人以外，所有人其实，嗯，都在隔间里办公，呃，包括那边的各位副总裁。格温就在她的隔间里。

segments.textEn: Um, I should have cleaned up if I were coming. Although this is really reality, I guess. I'm responsible for sales. I'm in charge of uh making sure that there's revenue here in the company and we're working on lots of Falcon 1 deals, Falcon 9 deals, and Dragon deals. So, this is just a little area where people can meet and um and have sort of an impromptu meeting. Um, obviously also very open. Um, I think it's actually quite helpful to have this openness because then you can sort of see what people are working on in their computers. Um like what Matt McCun here is is doing. Um what are you working on there? Uh I'm making a uh assembly documentation for the uh Draco. Okay. RCS. David is is driving the development of our inspace thruster which is called Draco. Um and um there's a little piece of it or that's just a temp that's just a sample spun cone. Yeah. So yeah, we're doing all our Texas testing at our facility down there. We got a new vacuum system.

segments.textEn: So kind of going back and forth between there kind of progress along. Right. We we named our copper frames after the great um rocket engineers and great scientists related to space. So we think they they really deserve the credit for you know enabling us to become a space fairing civilization. So we're fairly um science and engineering centric. Um we have some some conference rooms named after astronauts too but but we try to focus more on the the people that actually designed and built the rocket.
segments.textZh: 所以就是在两边来回跑，随着进展推进。对。所以，这台直连发动机用于我们的 Dragon 航天器，也用于 Falcon 9 的上面级，执行轨道机动和再入。这是，呃，我们的会议室、VIP 会议室，呃，用于会见客户，以及，嗯，如果某位客户的 CEO 来访之类的情况。它挺酷的，因为这里装了这种玻璃，嗯，可以变得不透明，而且我们在上面安装了运动传感器。所以当你走进去时，玻璃就会变得不透明。我们用伟大的，嗯，火箭工程师和与太空有关的伟大科学家的名字来命名我们的铜制框架。所以我们认为，正是他们让我们能够成为一个航天文明，他们确实应该获得赞誉。所以我们相当，嗯，以科学和工程为中心。嗯，我们也有一些会议室以宇航员命名，但我们尽量更多地关注那些真正设计和制造火箭的人。
